title: Phase-Stable Hologram Updates for Large-Scale Neutral-Atom Array Reconfiguration
summary: Dynamic holographic optical tweezers provide a programmable route to array assembly and reconfiguration essential for scalable neutral-atom quantum computation. However, phase mismatch between successive holograms can cause destructive interference during finite spatial light modulator (SLM) refresh. In this work, we analyze finite SLM refresh to establish a phase-stability criterion for prescribed trap amplitudes and develop a weighted-projective Gerchberg-Saxton (WPGS) method that efficiently approximates the corresponding phase-only complex-field optimization.
